offense_class: Misdemeanor (first/second); Class C Felony (third); Class B Felony (fourth+)
elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
On a public highway or street
While under the influence of alcohol, a controlled substance, or any substance that impairs mental or physical faculties
Or had a BAC of .08 or higher
enhancements: Child under 14 in vehicle (Class C Felony under § 32-5A-191(q))
Third conviction within 5 years (Class C Felony)
Fourth or subsequent conviction (Class B Felony)
notes: Implied consent under § 32-5-192. Admin license suspension 90 days first offense. Ignition interlock may be ordered. Community service required for most offenses.

elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol or controlled substances
BAC .08 or higher, or impairment of normal faculties
No prior DUI convictions
mandatory_minimum: Minimum 1 year license suspension; completion of court-approved substance abuse program
notes: Eligible for hardship license after 45 days. Must attend DUI or substance abuse program at defendant's expense.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (second); Class C Felony (third); Class B Felony (fourth+)
penalty_min: 5 days or 30 days community service (second); 60 days (third); 1 year and 1 day (fourth+)
elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol or controlled substances
BAC .08 or higher, or impairment of normal faculties
One or more prior DUI convictions
mandatory_minimum: 5 days imprisonment or 30 days community service (second); 60 days imprisonment (third); 1 year and 1 day imprisonment (fourth+)
enhancements: Refusal to submit to chemical test
notes: Second offense: 1-year license revocation. Third offense: 3-year revocation. Fourth+: 5-year revocation. Ignition interlock required for repeat offenders.

offense_class: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
penalty_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
fine_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of a controlled substance
Or under the combined influence of alcohol and a controlled substance
To a degree which renders the defendant incapable of safely driving
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
enhancements: Combined influence of alcohol and drugs
Presence of Schedule I substance in blood/urine
notes: No per se limit for drugs. Prosecution must show actual impairment. Includes prescription medications that impair driving ability.

elements: Defendant drove a vehicle
In willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property
notes: Common plea-down from DUI. Adds 6 points to driving record.

statute_title: Duty to Stop at Scene of Accident — Injury or Death
offense_class: Class C Felony (injury/death); Class A Misdemeanor (property damage only under § 32-10-2)
elements: Defendant was the driver of a vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in injury, death, or property damage
Defendant failed to stop at the scene
Defendant failed to provide identification and render aid
notes: Leaving the scene involving death or serious injury is a Class C Felony. Property damage only is Class A Misdemeanor.

elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol or controlled substances
Proximately caused the death of another person
notes: Alabama charges DUI-related deaths under the DUI statute with death-resulting enhancement, or under reckless murder/manslaughter statutes.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
By criminal negligence
While operating a motor vehicle
notes: Alabama does not have a separate vehicular manslaughter statute. Vehicular deaths may be charged as criminally negligent homicide (Class A Misdemeanor) or reckless manslaughter (Class B Felony) depending on culpability.

statute_title: Driving While License Canceled, Suspended, or Revoked
offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (subsequent)
elements: Defendant drove a motor vehicle on a public road
Defendant's license was canceled, suspended, or revoked
Defendant had knowledge of the suspension or revocation
notes: License suspension for DUI is separate from criminal penalties. Additional 6-month suspension for driving on suspended.

statute_title: Attempting to Elude a Police Officer
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (basic); Class B Felony (if serious injury or death results)
elements: A law enforcement officer signaled the defendant to stop
Signal was given by hand, voice, siren, or light
Defendant willfully failed to stop
Defendant attempted to flee or elude the officer
enhancements: Serious physical injury results (Class B Felony)
notes: Officer must be in uniform and operating a marked vehicle, or defendant must have reasonable knowledge the person is a law enforcement officer.

offense_class: Class C Felony (most controlled substances); Class A Misdemeanor (marijuana second degree)
elements: Defendant possessed a controlled substance
Substance is listed in Alabama Uniform Controlled Substances Act schedules
Possession was without a valid prescription or lawful authority
enhancements: Possession near a public housing project (§ 13A-12-270)
notes: Alabama classifies simple possession of most Schedule I-V substances as a Class C Felony. Marijuana has separate lesser provisions.

statute_title: Unlawful Possession of Marijuana — Second Degree
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first, personal use); Class C Felony (second+)
elements: Defendant possessed marijuana
For personal use only (not for sale)
Without lawful authority
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (Class C Felony)
Possession of more than personal use quantity
notes: First offense personal use marijuana is Class A Misdemeanor. Second or subsequent becomes Class C Felony. Alabama does not have legal recreational marijuana.

elements: Defendant possessed cocaine
Cocaine is a Schedule II controlled substance in Alabama
Possession was without lawful authority
notes: No quantity threshold needed for possession charge. Larger quantities may support trafficking charges under § 13A-12-231.

elements: Defendant possessed methamphetamine
Methamphetamine is a Schedule II controlled substance
Possession was without lawful authority
notes: Methamphetamine possession charged under the general controlled substance possession statute. Manufacturing is a separate Class B Felony.

elements: Defendant knowingly sold, manufactured, delivered, or possessed
A controlled substance in a quantity meeting trafficking thresholds
Specific weight thresholds vary by substance
mandatory_minimum: 3 years and $50,000 fine (cannabis 2.2-100 lbs); 5 years and $50,000 fine (cocaine 28g-500g); 3 years and $50,000 fine (meth 28g-500g)
enhancements: Higher quantity tiers carry enhanced mandatory minimums
notes: Alabama has some of the harshest trafficking penalties in the nation. Mandatory minimums cannot be suspended or probated. Weight thresholds: cannabis 2.2 lbs, cocaine 28g, meth 28g, heroin 4g.

elements: Defendant sold, furnished, gave away, delivered, or distributed
A controlled substance listed in Schedules I-V
Without lawful authority
enhancements: Distribution near a public housing project (§ 13A-12-270)
notes: Includes sale, gift, and delivery. Distribution to a minor is a Class A Felony.

statute_title: Unlawful Manufacturing of Controlled Substance — First Degree
elements: Defendant manufactured, produced, or created a controlled substance
Or possessed precursors with intent to manufacture
Without lawful authority
enhancements: Manufacturing meth (enhanced under Chemical Endangerment Act § 26-15-3.2)
notes: Chemical Endangerment Act (§ 26-15-3.2) provides additional severe penalties when children are exposed to manufacturing environments.

elements: Defendant possessed drug paraphernalia
With knowledge that it was to be used for a controlled substance
Paraphernalia as defined in § 13A-12-260(a)
enhancements: Delivery or sale of paraphernalia (Class A Misdemeanor)
Delivery to a minor (Class B Felony)
notes: Paraphernalia includes pipes, bongs, syringes (when used for illicit drugs), scales, and baggies. Context determines whether an item is paraphernalia.

elements: Defendant possessed a controlled substance
With the intent to sell, deliver, or distribute
Without lawful authority
notes: Intent can be inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, large amounts of cash, and other circumstantial evidence.

offense_class: Class A Felony (Capital if aggravating factors under § 13A-5-40)
penalty_min: Life (non-capital); death or life without parole (capital)
penalty_max: Death (capital); life without parole; life with possibility of parole
elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
With the intent to cause the death of that person or another
Or under circumstances manifesting extreme indifference to human life
enhancements: Murder during commission of a felony (felony murder)
notes: Alabama is a death penalty state. Capital murder requires at least one aggravating circumstance from § 13A-5-40. Judge makes final sentencing decision after jury recommendation.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
Under circumstances manifesting extreme indifference to human life
Defendant recklessly engaged in conduct creating grave risk of death
notes: Alabama technically has a single murder statute with different theories. What other states call second-degree murder is prosecuted as depraved-heart murder under § 13A-6-2(a)(2).

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
The killing was committed under the influence of extreme emotional disturbance
For which there was a reasonable explanation or excuse
notes: Alabama does not use the term 'voluntary manslaughter' but the heat-of-passion manslaughter provision serves the same function. Burden on defendant to raise adequate provocation.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
By reckless conduct
Defendant was aware of and consciously disregarded a substantial risk
notes: Covers what most states call involuntary manslaughter. Class B Felony — notably harsh compared to other states.

elements: Defendant caused serious physical injury to another person
With intent to cause serious physical injury
Or caused serious physical injury by means of a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument
notes: Alabama's first-degree assault is the equivalent of aggravated assault in most other states. Serious physical injury means substantial risk of death, protracted disfigurement, or protracted impairment.

elements: Defendant caused physical injury to another person
Or with criminal negligence caused physical injury by means of a deadly weapon
notes: Third-degree assault covers simple assault situations. Second-degree assault (§ 13A-6-21, Class C Felony) fills the gap between first and third degree.

elements: Defendant caused physical injury to another person
Intent to cause physical injury, or reckless conduct, or criminal negligence with a weapon
notes: Alabama merged assault and battery into a single assault offense. There is no separate battery statute.

elements: Defendant committed a theft
Defendant used force or threatened imminent use of force
Against the person of the owner or another person present
notes: Alabama has three degrees of robbery. Third degree is the base offense. Second degree (§ 13A-8-42) involves being aided by another person. First degree (§ 13A-8-41) involves serious injury or use of a deadly weapon.

elements: Defendant committed a robbery
Defendant was armed with a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument
Or caused serious physical injury to another person
notes: Class A Felony. Armed with a deadly weapon or causing serious injury elevates robbery to first degree.

elements: Defendant abducted another person
With intent to hold for ransom, use as a shield or hostage, terrorize, or commit a felony
Or restrained the person under circumstances exposing them to serious physical injury
notes: Second-degree kidnapping (§ 13A-6-44) is a Class B Felony involving abduction with intent to inflict physical injury or violate sexual offenses.

elements: Defendant intentionally damaged a building
By starting or maintaining a fire or causing an explosion
When another person was present in the building
Defendant knew or should have known a person might be present
notes: Three degrees of arson. First degree requires a person present. Second degree (§ 13A-7-42, Class B Felony) is damage to a building. Third degree (§ 13A-7-43, Class C Felony) is damage to property.

elements: Defendant intended to cause the death of another person
Defendant engaged in conduct constituting a substantial step toward the commission of murder
Conduct was strongly corroborative of the criminal intent
enhancements: Victim is a law enforcement officer
notes: Charged under the general attempt statute (§ 13A-4-2) combined with murder. An attempt to commit a Class A Felony is itself a Class A Felony in Alabama.

statute_title: Assault — First Degree with Deadly Weapon
elements: Defendant caused serious physical injury to another
By means of a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument
With intent to cause serious physical injury
notes: Covered under first-degree assault. Deadly weapon defined in § 13A-1-2(7) as any firearm or object that is likely to cause death or serious physical injury.

offense_class: Class B Felony (over $2,500); Class C Felony ($500-$2,500); Class A Misdemeanor (under $500)
penalty_max: 20 years (first degree); 10 years (second degree); 1 year (third degree)
elements: Defendant knowingly obtained or exerted unauthorized control over the property of another
With intent to deprive the owner of the property
enhancements: Theft of a firearm (automatic first degree regardless of value)
notes: Threshold: Over $2,500 = first degree (Class B Felony), $500-$2,500 = second degree (Class C Felony), under $500 = third degree (Class A Misdemeanor). Theft of a firearm is always first degree.

elements: Defendant knowingly obtained or exerted unauthorized control over property
Value of property exceeds $2,500
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Alabama uses the 'theft of property' framework with degree-based thresholds rather than 'grand theft' terminology.

elements: Defendant knowingly obtained or exerted unauthorized control over property
Value of property is less than $500
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Under $500 threshold. Fourth or subsequent conviction for theft of property fourth degree can be upgraded.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (under $500); Class C Felony ($500-$2,500); Class B Felony (over $2,500)
penalty_max: 1 year (misdemeanor); 10 years (Class C Felony); 20 years (Class B Felony)
elements: Defendant concealed, removed, or altered merchandise
Of a retail establishment
With intent to deprive the merchant of value without paying
enhancements: Use of booster bags or devices
notes: Typically charged under the general theft statutes. Penalties follow the same degree structure as theft of property.

elements: Defendant knowingly entered or remained unlawfully
In a building
With intent to commit a crime therein
notes: Three degrees. Third degree: entry into a building. Second degree (§ 13A-7-6): entry into a dwelling. First degree (§ 13A-7-5): entry into a dwelling while armed or causing injury.

elements: Defendant knowingly entered or remained unlawfully
In a dwelling
With intent to commit a crime therein
enhancements: Armed with a deadly weapon or explosive (elevates to first degree)
Causes physical injury (elevates to first degree)
Uses or threatens use of a dangerous instrument
notes: Dwelling includes any building used for overnight lodging. First-degree burglary (§ 13A-7-5) is a Class A Felony when armed, causing injury, or using explosives.

statute_title: Theft of Property — First Degree (Motor Vehicle)
elements: Defendant knowingly obtained or exerted unauthorized control over a motor vehicle
With intent to deprive the owner of the vehicle
Value exceeds $2,500
notes: No separate motor vehicle theft statute. Charged as first-degree theft due to value. Joyriding may be charged as unauthorized use of a vehicle under § 13A-8-11.

offense_class: Class B Felony (over $2,500); Class C Felony ($500-$2,500); Class A Misdemeanor (under $500)
penalty_max: 20 years (Class B); 10 years (Class C); 1 year (Class A Misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant received, retained, or disposed of stolen property
Knowing that it was stolen or having reasonable grounds to believe it was stolen
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Degree structure mirrors theft: first degree over $2,500, second degree $500-$2,500, third degree under $500.

offense_class: Class C Felony (over $2,500 damage); Class A Misdemeanor (under $2,500)
penalty_max: 10 years (Class C Felony); 1 year (Class A Misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant intentionally damaged the property of another person
Without the owner's consent
Damage exceeds $2,500 (first degree) or involves a dwelling, utility, or explosive
enhancements: Damage to church or religious facility (§ 13A-11-12)
notes: Alabama uses 'criminal mischief' rather than 'vandalism' as the statutory term. Three degrees based on damage amount and circumstances.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first degree); Class C Misdemeanor (third degree)
elements: Defendant knowingly entered or remained unlawfully
In a dwelling (first degree) or building (second degree) or fenced/enclosed property (third degree)
notes: Three degrees. First degree (dwelling) is Class A Misdemeanor. Second degree (building) is Class B Misdemeanor. Third degree (premises) is Class C Misdemeanor.

elements: Defendant intentionally damaged property of another
Damage exceeds $2,500 in value
Without consent of the owner
enhancements: Damage to utility or communication property
notes: First degree requires over $2,500 damage or interruption of public service. Second degree (§ 13A-7-22) is $500-$2,500 (Class A Misdemeanor). Third degree (§ 13A-7-23) is under $500 (Class B Misdemeanor).

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (third degree); Class B Felony (first degree); Class C Felony (second degree)
penalty_max: 1 year (third degree); 20 years (first degree); 10 years (second degree)
elements: Defendant committed an assault, menacing, reckless endangerment, criminal coercion, harassment, or stalking
Against a current or former spouse, parent of a common child, household member, or dating partner
enhancements: Use of a deadly weapon (first degree)
notes: Alabama's domestic violence statutes (§ 13A-6-130 through 13A-6-139) mirror the three-degree assault structure applied to domestic relationships. Mandatory arrest provisions apply.

elements: Defendant caused serious physical injury to a household member or intimate partner
With intent to cause serious physical injury
Or caused serious physical injury with a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument
notes: Alabama merges assault and battery concepts. First-degree domestic violence covers what many states call domestic battery with serious injury.

statute_title: Chemical Endangerment of Exposing a Child to an Environment of Controlled Substance
offense_class: Class C Felony (exposure); Class A Felony (serious injury); Class A Felony (death)
elements: Defendant knowingly, recklessly, or intentionally caused or permitted
A child to be exposed to, ingested, inhaled, or had contact with
A controlled substance, chemical substance, or drug paraphernalia
enhancements: Child suffers serious physical injury (Class A Felony)
notes: Alabama's chemical endangerment statute has been controversially applied to pregnant women who use drugs. Also see general endangering the welfare of a child under § 13A-13-6.

offense_class: Class B Felony (abuse); Class A Felony (aggravated)
elements: Defendant tortured, willfully abused, cruelly beat, or otherwise willfully maltreated
A child under the age of 18
enhancements: Serious physical injury (aggravated, Class A Felony)
notes: Simple child abuse (§ 26-15-3) is a Class B Felony. Aggravated child abuse with serious injury is a Class A Felony.

statute_title: Violation of a Domestic Violence Protection Order
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Class C Felony (second+)
elements: A valid protection order was in effect
Defendant had notice of the protection order
Defendant willfully violated a condition of the order
enhancements: Second or subsequent violation (Class C Felony)
Violation involving physical force or threat
notes: First violation is a Class A Misdemeanor. Second or subsequent violations become Class C Felonies. Violation with assault may be charged under domestic violence statutes.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first); Class B Felony (second offense or violating protection order)
elements: Defendant intentionally and repeatedly followed or harassed another person
Defendant made a credible threat with intent to place that person in reasonable fear
Of death or serious bodily harm
enhancements: Violation of protection order while stalking (Class B Felony)
notes: Aggravated stalking (§ 13A-6-91) applies when done in violation of a protection order or after a prior stalking conviction.

elements: Defendant with intent to harass, annoy, or alarm another person
Struck, shoved, kicked another person, or subjected them to physical contact
Or directed abusive or obscene language or made an obscene gesture toward another
notes: Harassment is a relatively minor offense. May be charged alongside or as a lesser-included offense of assault. Separate provisions for electronic harassment.

statute_title: Abuse, Neglect, or Exploitation of a Protected Person
offense_class: Class C Felony (abuse/neglect); Class B Felony (exploitation over $500)
elements: Defendant abused, neglected, or exploited a protected person
Protected person is elderly (60+) or otherwise vulnerable adult
Defendant was a caregiver or had a duty of care
notes: Protected persons include those 60+ and incapacitated adults. Exploitation includes financial exploitation. Mandatory reporting requirements under § 38-9-8.

statute_title: Certain Persons Forbidden to Possess Firearm
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm
Defendant was a convicted felon, had been adjudicated mentally defective, or was subject to a domestic violence protection order
notes: Alabama is a permitless carry state as of January 2023. The primary weapons restriction is for prohibited persons. Short-barreled rifles/shotguns and destructive devices are regulated under § 13A-11-63.

statute_title: Possession of Firearm by Convicted Felon
elements: Defendant possessed, owned, or had under control a firearm or destructive device
Defendant had been convicted of a crime of violence as defined in § 13A-11-70
notes: Crime of violence is defined in § 13A-11-70. Alabama's permitless carry law does not change prohibitions for convicted felons.

statute_title: Possession of Firearm by Prohibited Person in Certain Places
offense_class: Class C Felony (prohibited person); varies for location violations
elements: Defendant carried a concealed weapon or firearm
In a location where firearms are prohibited (courthouse, school, etc.)
Or defendant was a prohibited person carrying a firearm
notes: Alabama adopted permitless carry in January 2023. Most concealed carry violations now relate to prohibited persons or prohibited locations rather than lack of a permit.

elements: Defendant discharged a firearm
In a reckless manner creating a risk of harm
Into an occupied dwelling, building, or vehicle, or into a public area
enhancements: Shooting into an occupied dwelling (§ 13A-11-61, Class B Felony)
notes: Shooting into an occupied dwelling, vehicle, or building is a Class B Felony under § 13A-11-61. Reckless discharge generally falls under reckless endangerment (§ 13A-6-24).

offense_class: Class C Felony (first offense); Class B Felony (second offense); Class A Felony (third+)
penalty_max: 10 years (Class C); 20 years (Class B); Life (Class A)
elements: Defendant obtained, recorded, or accessed the identifying information of another person
Without authorization and with fraudulent intent
Used or attempted to use the information to obtain anything of value
notes: Alabama escalates identity theft with each subsequent offense. Victim restitution is mandatory.

offense_class: Same as theft by degree (Class B Felony over $2,500; Class C Felony $500-$2,500; Class A Misdemeanor under $500)
penalty_max: 20 years (Class B); 10 years (Class C); 1 year (Class A Misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant was entrusted with property of another
Defendant knowingly converted the property to their own use
Without consent of the owner
notes: Charged under the general theft statute. The manner of taking (embezzlement/conversion by a trusted party) is a theory, not a separate crime.

offense_class: Class C Felony (first degree); Class A Misdemeanor (second degree)
elements: Defendant falsely made, completed, or altered a written instrument
With intent to defraud or deceive
Instrument is or purports to be a government-issued document, deed, will, contract, or financial instrument
notes: First-degree forgery covers government documents, securities, and financial instruments. Second-degree forgery (§ 13A-9-3) covers other documents.

statute_title: Criminal Possession of a Forged Instrument — First Degree
elements: Defendant possessed a forged instrument
With knowledge that it was forged
With intent to defraud, deceive, or injure another
notes: Counterfeiting of currency is primarily a federal offense. State charges typically involve forged documents or instruments.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (under $500); Class C Felony ($500-$2,500); Class B Felony (over $2,500)
elements: Defendant issued or passed a check, draft, or order for payment of money
Knowing there were insufficient funds
With intent to defraud
notes: Degree determined by amount. The defendant must receive notice of dishonor and fail to make good within 10 days for criminal prosecution.

offense_class: Class C Felony (under $500); Class B Felony ($500+)
elements: Defendant made a false statement or representation
In connection with an insurance claim
With intent to defraud an insurer
notes: Includes filing false claims, staged accidents, and inflating damages. Mandatory restitution and potential civil penalties.

statute_title: Fraudulent Use of a Credit or Debit Card
offense_class: Class C Felony (over $500); Class A Misdemeanor (under $500)
elements: Defendant used a credit or debit card
Knowing it was stolen, forged, revoked, or canceled
With intent to defraud the card issuer or merchant
notes: Includes using a stolen card, forged card, or card obtained by fraud. Possession of multiple stolen cards is a separate offense.

fine_max: $250,000 or twice the value of the property involved
elements: Defendant conducted or attempted to conduct a financial transaction
Involving proceeds of unlawful activity
With knowledge that the property involved represents proceeds of some form of unlawful activity
With intent to promote the carrying on of unlawful activity or to conceal the source
notes: Alabama's money laundering statute is found within the drug trafficking chapter but applies broadly. Federal charges are also common.

offense_class: Same as theft by degree based on value
elements: Defendant obtained property of another by deception
Created or confirmed a false impression of fact or law
Or failed to correct a false impression previously created
notes: General fraud is charged as theft by deception under the theft statutes. Degree follows the standard value thresholds.

elements: Defendant subjected another person to sexual contact
By forcible compulsion
Or the victim was incapable of consent due to physical helplessness or mental incapacity
notes: Alabama uses 'sexual abuse' rather than 'sexual assault' for non-penetration offenses. First-degree rape (§ 13A-6-61) covers penetration offenses.

elements: Defendant engaged in sexual intercourse with another person
By forcible compulsion
Or the victim was incapable of consent by reason of physical helplessness or mental incapacity
Or victim was less than 12 years old
notes: First-degree rape is a Class A Felony. Second-degree (§ 13A-6-62) involves victims aged 12-16 when defendant is 16+ and at least 2 years older. SORNA registration required.

elements: Defendant exposed their private parts in a public place
Or where the act could be observed by others
With intent to arouse or gratify sexual desire, or to affront or alarm
enhancements: Exposure to a minor (elevated charges possible)
notes: Alabama uses 'public lewdness' rather than indecent exposure. Exposure to children may result in more serious charges under sexual abuse statutes.

elements: Defendant offered to engage in or agreed to engage in sexual conduct
In exchange for money or other consideration
Or solicited another to engage in prostitution
enhancements: Solicitation of a minor (elevated felony charges)
notes: Both the person offering and the person soliciting can be charged. Promoting prostitution (§ 13A-12-111) is a Class C Felony.

statute_title: Possession of Obscene Material Depicting a Minor
offense_class: Class C Felony (possession); Class B Felony (distribution); Class A Felony (production)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed material depicting a minor engaged in obscene acts
Defendant knew or should have known the subject was a minor
notes: Federal charges are common in addition to state charges. SORNA registration required upon conviction.

statute_title: Failure to Register as Sex Offender
elements: Defendant was required to register as a sex offender under ACNA
Defendant failed to register or update registration as required
Defendant acted knowingly
notes: Alabama Community Notification Act (ACNA) requires registration. Must register within 3 business days of establishing residence. Electronic monitoring may be required.

elements: Defendant engaged in sexual intercourse with another person
Victim was between 12 and 16 years old
Defendant was 16 years or older and at least 2 years older than the victim
notes: Age of consent in Alabama is 16. No close-in-age (Romeo and Juliet) exception. SORNA registration required.

elements: Defendant with intent to cause public inconvenience, annoyance, or alarm
Or recklessly creating a risk thereof
Engaged in fighting, violent, tumultuous, or threatening behavior
Or made unreasonable noise, or used abusive or obscene language in public
notes: Common add-on charge. Often paired with resisting arrest or public intoxication.

elements: Defendant intentionally prevented or attempted to prevent a law enforcement officer
From effecting a lawful arrest of the defendant or another person
enhancements: Use of force or violence (may upgrade charges)
notes: Defense may argue the arrest was unlawful. Physical resistance that causes injury may lead to additional assault charges.

elements: Defendant intentionally obstructed, impaired, or hindered
The administration of law or other governmental function
By means of intimidation, force, violence, or physical interference
notes: Broader than resisting arrest — covers interference with any governmental function, including court proceedings and investigations.

offense_class: Varies (civil or criminal; summary or constructive)
elements: Defendant willfully disobeyed a lawful order of the court
Or engaged in disruptive behavior in the courtroom
Or failed to appear as ordered
notes: Criminal contempt is punitive; civil contempt is coercive. Judge has broad discretion. Right to jury trial for serious criminal contempt (over 6 months possible).

elements: Defendant appeared in a public place
Under the influence of alcohol, a controlled substance, or any substance
To the degree that the defendant endangered themselves, others, or property
Or by boisterous or indecent conduct annoys others in the vicinity
notes: Classified as a violation, not a misdemeanor. However, still results in arrest and can impact other pending cases.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (misdemeanor case); Class C Felony (felony case)
elements: Defendant was released on bail or personal recognizance
Required to appear at a specified time and place
Defendant intentionally failed to appear as required
enhancements: Underlying charge is a felony (Class C Felony)
notes: Bench warrant issued upon failure to appear. Bond forfeiture in addition to criminal charges. Separate from contempt of court.

elements: Defendant reported false information to law enforcement
Knowing the information to be false
Regarding a crime or emergency
notes: Includes false reports of crimes, emergencies, or incidents. May also implicate filing a false police report under § 13A-10-9.

elements: Defendant by physical action intentionally placed or attempted to place another person
In fear of imminent serious physical injury
notes: Alabama uses 'menacing' rather than 'criminal threat' or 'terroristic threat.' Threats communicated verbally may fall under harassment (§ 13A-11-8) or intimidation statutes.

elements: Defendant made a false sworn statement
In an official proceeding
The statement was material to the proceeding
Defendant did not believe the statement to be true
notes: First-degree perjury applies in official proceedings. Second-degree (§ 13A-10-102) applies to other sworn statements.

elements: Defendant offered, conferred, or agreed to confer a benefit
Upon a public servant
With intent to influence the public servant's official action
notes: Both the giver and receiver can be charged. Receiving a bribe (§ 13A-10-62) is also a Class C Felony.

elements: Defendant escaped from custody
While charged with or convicted of a felony
Using physical force or threat of physical force
enhancements: Use of a weapon during escape
notes: Three degrees of escape. First degree involves force while in felony custody. Second degree (§ 13A-10-32) is felony custody without force. Third degree (§ 13A-10-33) is misdemeanor custody.

offense_class: Class C Felony (first degree); Class A Misdemeanor (second degree)
elements: Defendant intentionally tortured, tormented, or mutilated an animal
Or caused unjustifiable pain or suffering
Resulting in serious physical injury or death to the animal
notes: First-degree cruelty involves intentional serious injury or death. Second-degree (§ 13A-11-14.1) covers general mistreatment. Dog fighting is a separate felony.

penalty_max: Remaining suspended sentence on underlying offense
elements: Defendant was placed on probation
Defendant violated a condition of probation
Violation was willful and material
enhancements: New criminal offense while on probation
notes: Judge has discretion to revoke, modify, or continue probation. Defendant entitled to hearing. Standard of proof is preponderance of the evidence.

elements: Defendant was released on parole
Defendant violated a condition of parole
Violation was established at a revocation hearing
notes: Board of Pardons and Paroles makes revocation decisions. Technical violations may result in graduated sanctions rather than full revocation.

elements: Defendant aided, abetted, counseled, or encouraged another person
In the commission of a crime
With the intent to promote or assist in the commission of the offense
notes: An accomplice is criminally liable to the same extent as the principal. Alabama's complicity statute eliminates the common-law distinctions between principals and accessories.

offense_class: One class below the attempted offense (Class A attempted = Class A attempt; Class B attempted = Class B attempt; etc.)
penalty_max: Varies by class of the attempted offense
fine_max: Varies by class of the attempted offense
elements: Defendant intended to commit a specific offense
Defendant engaged in conduct constituting a substantial step toward commission
The conduct was strongly corroborative of the criminal intent
notes: Attempt to commit a Class A Felony is a Class A Felony. Attempt to commit a Class B Felony is a Class B Felony. Exception: attempt to commit a murder is always a Class A Felony.

offense_class: One class below the target offense
penalty_max: Varies by class of target offense
fine_max: Varies by class of target offense
elements: Defendant agreed with one or more persons to engage in conduct constituting a crime
Defendant or a co-conspirator committed an overt act in furtherance of the agreement
Defendant intended that the crime be committed
notes: Conspiracy to commit a Class A Felony is a Class B Felony. Requires at least one overt act. Withdrawal is a defense if communicated to co-conspirators before the overt act.
